model_output.cross_horizon_summary: The latest BTC/ETH rebound provides tactical support, but does not establish continuation or broad altcoin recovery. The 12h horizon has no clean directional edge; the 72h horizon leans DOWN with low confidence because liquidity contraction, settled ETF outflows and weaker participation challenge rebound durability. The 168h terminal direction remains NO_EDGE rather than an extrapolation of near-term pressure. Altcoin transmission is weak and proxy-only. These are descriptive, non-binding forecasts with no execution, portfolio-sizing or framework-change authority.
global_missing_evidence: Durable, source-qualified broad-alt and large-cap breadth confirmation; both canonical breadth states remain UNCONFIRMED.
Full small-cap coverage and any observed microcap transmission lane; Top-100 tail performance cannot establish either.
Multi-session spot-flow, price and derivatives histories sufficient to distinguish persistent demand from a temporary rebound.
Stablecoin deployment confirmation; supply changes alone do not establish buying or selling.
Verified catalyst context is degraded. This is uncertainty, not bearish evidence.
Live-anchor source-observation freshness is unavailable despite passing retrieval checks; the supplied observations also have different timestamps and cadences.

contradicting_evidence: The completed hourly candle shows BTC up 0.321%, ETH up 0.571% and ETH/BTC up 0.250%, providing a coherent immediate upside impulse.
BTC taker-buy quote share was 60.36%, supporting the possibility of further near-term gains.
Current breadth remains net positive at 59% advancing, rather than showing broad outright contraction.
12h.expected_path: A near-term rebound can persist, particularly in BTC, but continuation is not sufficiently established to distinguish it from a rebound that retraces. Expect an unresolved, potentially choppy contest between immediate price strength and fragile participation. NO_EDGE is not a low-volatility or flat-price forecast.
falsification_conditions: An upside edge would emerge if subsequent completed candles sustain gains alongside persistent spot buying, stronger ETH/BTC and broader participation.
A downside edge would emerge if the latest hourly gains unwind while spot selling and breadth deterioration persist.
The relevance of the earlier ask-heavy depth snapshot would diminish if refreshed books show that supply clearing alongside sustained price follow-through.
missing_evidence: Several subsequent completed hourly observations to establish persistence rather than a single-candle impulse.
Refreshed order books and cross-venue spot-flow confirmation; the available depth snapshot predates the completed hourly candle.
Hourly funding-event rates and a longer, comparable open-interest history.
supporting_evidence: Breadth fell by 21 percentage points versus the prior packet even as BTC and ETH rose, weakening the case for broad continuation.

BTC price rose with open interest down 0.151%, which does not establish fresh leveraged demand. ETH price rose with open interest up 1.743%, but its taker-buy quote share was only 42.99%; absorption is possible, recovery is not proven.

Earlier single-venue depth was sharply ask-heavy for both BTC and ETH, while BTC trade imbalance was positive. These conflicting, asynchronous observations do not establish persistent supply or demand.
The aggregate median 24h return was only 0.160% versus a 1.346% mean, indicating that the headline gain was not representative of the typical constituent.

contradicting_evidence: Stablecoin supply contraction over seven and thirty days, together with the latest settled ETF outflows, creates a credible downside alternative rather than a balanced fundamental backdrop.
Positive BTC/ETH price action, improving ETH/BTC and selective Top-100 tail participation create a credible recovery alternative if they persist.
168h.expected_path: There is insufficient evidence for a defensible week-end direction. Continued liquidity pressure could keep rebounds fragile, while persistent spot demand and improving participation could support repair. Neither branch is confirmed, and no turning day or recovery sequence is supported.
falsification_conditions: Replace NO_EDGE with an upside assessment if repeated sessions show durable price strength, sustained ETH/BTC improvement, source-qualified breadth expansion and improving flows together.
Replace NO_EDGE with a downside assessment if repeated sessions establish lower prices alongside persistent breadth contraction and continued liquidity or ETF-flow weakness.
A BTC-only advance without wider relative-strength participation would not establish broad altcoin recovery.
missing_evidence: The next sequence of settled ETF sessions and stablecoin observations needed to test whether current flow pressure persists.
A durable breadth and ETH/BTC trend rather than isolated positive observations.
Verified upcoming catalyst information and refreshed macro observations.
Independent coverage beyond the Top-100 proxy universe.
supporting_evidence: The supplied evidence combines a short-lived positive price impulse with slower negative liquidity evidence; neither establishes persistence through a full week.
Altseason readings are between published thresholds, while only 30.6% of the observed 30-day alt basket outperformed BTC. This does not confirm a broad rotation regime.
The stronger Top-100 tail proxy has 65.2% advancing, but its 2.276% mean return exceeds its 0.861% median substantially. Selective strength does not establish full small-cap or microcap transmission.
The structural prior provides conditional scenarios, not a verified weekly path or independent confirmation of a turning point.

contradicting_evidence: BTC and ETH have positive hourly and 24h returns, and ETH/BTC improved in the latest completed hour.
BTC spot buying is supportive, while positive breadth and selective smaller-asset strength leave room for a broader relief rally.
Stablecoin supply was slightly positive over one day, so the slower contraction is not evidence of uninterrupted daily withdrawal.
The settled ETF figures describe the November 20 session and are unchanged from the prior packet; they are not fresh intraday outflows.
72h.expected_path: A low-confidence downside bias favors renewed pressure on rebound attempts over a durable broad recovery. Intermittent BTC/ETH strength can coexist with this path. Stabilization or apparent absorption would not, by itself, overturn the downside assessment.
falsification_conditions: Sustained price follow-through accompanied by improving spot demand and durable ETH/BTC strength would weaken the downside bias.
Source-qualified breadth expansion with stronger large- and mid-alt participation would contradict the present weak-transmission assessment.
Improving subsequent settled ETF flows and stabilization of the stablecoin supply trend would undermine the liquidity-pressure thesis.
missing_evidence: New settled ETF sessions to determine whether the latest negative session persists or reverses.
Repeated breadth observations and independent confirmation of broad participation.
Evidence that stablecoin supply is being deployed into risk assets.
Fresh macro observations; the supplied yields and VIX are slow context, not evidence of an ongoing intraday shock.
supporting_evidence: Stablecoin supply declined 1.584% over seven days and 6.166% over thirty days, providing a liquidity headwind despite the small positive one-day change.
The latest final ETF session recorded BTC outflows of $124.5 million and ETH outflows of $13.2 million, offering no institutional-flow confirmation of recovery.
The selected breadth observation is 59%, down 21 percentage points versus the prior packet. Only 42 of 100 constituents outperformed BTC and 36 outperformed ETH.
Large- and mid-alt proxy advance ratios are only about 53% and 52%; large-alt median performance trails BTC. Stronger Top-100 tail performance does not establish broad transmission.
The supplied 10-year yield of 5.04% and VIX of 28.44 describe a challenging risk backdrop, although their levels do not establish a new deterioration.
The freshest breadth point is used once. The aggregate and capitalization buckets share an upstream family and are not independent confirming votes.
